name: Niger
headline: Niger: +6.9% growth in 2025, −4.7% inflation, debt 46% of GDP
sections: Niger is a $21.3 billion economy (2025), the world's 134th-largest of 215 measured. Real output grew +6.9% in 2025, faster than the world median of +3.5%. Income per person is $2,177 at purchasing-power parity (2025), against a world median of $21K. Manufacturing accounts for 7.0% of GDP (2024).
Consumer prices rose −4.7% in 2025, in deflation, down from 4.2% in 2022. Unemployment stood at 0.4% (2025), below the world median of 5.1%. Youth unemployment was 0.5% (2025).
Gross government debt is 46% of GDP (2025), a moderate level. The general government balance is −2.9% of GDP (2025).
The current account balance is −3.7% of GDP (2025). Trade equals 34% of GDP (2025), a relatively closed economy. Net FDI inflows were 1.2% of GDP (2025).
IMF projections put government debt at 43% of GDP by 2031, broadly stable from today's level. Life expectancy is 61.4 years (2024). Population: 29.1 million (2025).
note: Built from official World Bank and IMF data; IMF projections are labelled as projections.
